introduction: Illinois TANF provides temporary cash and supportive services for eligible pregnant women and families with dependent children. Apply through IDHS.
description: Illinois TANF provides temporary cash and supportive services for eligible pregnant women and families with dependent children. Apply through IDHS.

sections.who: Applicants must live in Illinois and meet the program’s financial and other rules. The state includes pregnancy or a child younger than 19; an 18-year-old child must attend high school full time. Applicants develop and follow a self-sufficiency plan.
sections.get: TANF can help with food, shelter, utilities and other basic expenses. Related services can support education, work and family stability.
sections.docs:
• Child, caregiver and household details.
  • Income and expense records.
  • Identification, residence and other case verification requested by IDHS.
sections.apply:
1. Start the request

    Use ABE or the Family Community Resource Center serving your area.

  2. Return requested evidence

    Provide accurate household information and complete intake.

  3. Discuss your plan

    Ask about the work, training or support activities assigned to your case.
sections.after: Eligible cash benefits are issued through Illinois Link. Follow the decision notice, case plan and reporting directions.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using Illinois TANF conditions and services, application options. Agency staff determine eligibility.

faqs: Yes. The state explicitly says homelessness does not by itself prevent TANF eligibility.
Can pregnancy qualify without another child?
The state includes qualifying pregnant applicants even without other children.
Is TANF the same as SNAP?
No. SNAP is food assistance with its own determination.
The state requires an 18-year-old dependent child to be a full-time high school student.
